questions.def: After 'used to' and 'did,' use the base form of the verb.
questions.question: He didn't use to ___ so much coffee.

questions.def: 'Neither' is always paired with 'nor' to show negation.
questions.question: Neither my brother ___ I like horror movies.

questions.def: Use 'don't' + verb for simple present negative sentences.
questions.question: I ___ what he said.

questions.def: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb (except 'be').
questions.question: She ___ ever late for work.

questions.def: 'No' is used before nouns to express negation of quantity.
questions.question: I have ___ money to buy that car.

questions.def: Use 'didn't' + verb for simple past negative sentences.
questions.question: I ___ the question.

questions.def: 'None' refers to zero out of a group of people or things.
questions.question: ___ of them wanted to go to the party.

questions.def: Use 'no' before uncountable nouns to indicate a lack of something.
questions.question: There is ___ milk left in the fridge.

questions.def: Use 'don't' + verb for simple present negative sentences with plural subjects.
questions.question: They ___ the answer.

questions.def: 'Didn't' is used to form the past simple negative.
questions.question: He ___ go to the gym yesterday.

questions.def: 'Doesn't' is used with 'he/she/it' to form the present simple negative.
questions.question: He ___ have any brothers or sisters.

questions.def: Use 'don't' + verb for simple present negative sentences with 'I'.
questions.question: I ___ to go.

questions.def: 'Aren't' is the contracted form of 'are not'.
questions.question: They ___ coming to the meeting.

questions.def: 'Isn't' is the contracted form of 'is not'.
questions.question: She ___ going to the concert.

questions.def: Use 'doesn't' with 'he/she/it', not 'don't'.
questions.question: He don't like to swim.

questions.def: Use 'am not' to negate the verb 'be' with the subject 'I'.
questions.question: I ___ a doctor.

questions.def: Use 'isn't' with uncountable nouns to indicate a lack of something.
questions.question: There ___ any sugar in my tea.

questions.def: 'Haven't' is the correct form of 'have not' for 'they'.
questions.question: They ___ finished their homework yet.

questions.def: The correct form is 'doesn't go'. Missing auxiliary verb.
questions.question: She not go to the store today.

questions.def: Use 'didn't' + verb for simple past negative sentences.
questions.question: I ___ my homework yesterday.

questions.def: 'Never' is used to express that something has not happened.
questions.question: I have ___ seen that movie before.

questions.def: 'Wasn't' is the correct past form of 'be' for 'he'.
questions.question: He ___ able to come to the party.

questions.def: Use 'weren't' with plural subjects, not 'wasn't'.
questions.question: They wasn't at home yesterday evening.

questions.def: Use 'doesn't have' with 'he/she/it' to show lack of possession.
questions.question: She ___ any pets.

questions.def: 'Weren't' is the past plural negative form of 'be'.
questions.question: There ___ many people at the meeting.

questions.def: 'Haven't' is the correct contraction of 'have not' to form present perfect.
questions.question: I ___ seen him before.

questions.def: Use 'been' after 'have never' to indicate a past experience.
questions.question: I have never ___ to Japan. It's my dream.

questions.def: 'Neither' is always paired with 'nor' to express a negative choice.
questions.question: Neither my sister ___ I want to go to the party.

questions.def: Use 'seen' (past participle) after 'have' in present perfect tense.
questions.question: I have ___ him nowhere since last year.

questions.def: 'Scarcely' implies a negative meaning; use 'any' with it.
questions.question: There's scarcely ___ milk left in the fridge.
